## Summary of Work So Far

### Completed Requirements
- **[R1] Trailing newline**: Named fields `{x}` and `{name:d}` correctly parse input ending with `\n`. The `.+?` pattern captures everything including newlines. Verified working.

- **[R2] Numeric indices**: Fixed by modifying `_to_group_name()` to prepend `'field_'` prefix when the group name starts with a digit. Now `{0}`, `{0:d}`, `{0}:{1}` all compile and parse correctly.

- **[R3] Sign specifiers**: `extract_format()` extracts `sign` from format strings like `+10d`, `-5d` before processing zero-padding and width. Sign is stored in result dict.

- **[R4] Alignment handling**: No regressions detected. All existing alignment tests pass (left, right, center, fill characters). The current implementation preserves verbose use cases.

- **[R5] Datetime functions**: Added public API:
  - `dt_format_to_regex(dt_format)` → compiled regex
  - `get_regex_for_datetime_format(dt_format)` → same, documented wrapper  
  - `strf_date_convert(match, fmt)` → reconstructs datetime string from match dict
  - `date_convert(string, match, ...)` → existing function, works with match objects
  - Internal `_datetime_format_to_regex_inner()` handles all C-style directives: %Y, %y, %m, %d, %H, %M, %S, %f, %z, %A, %a, %B, %b, %h, %p, %%

- **[R6] Parser.format property**: Returns `self._format`, the original format string.

- **[R7] Variable-length %f**: Pattern `(\d{1,6})` matches 1-6 digits after decimal point. Works for milliseconds, microseconds, etc.

- **[R8] Hyphen-minus in field names**: `PARSE_RE` allows `[\\w-]*` in field names. `_to_group_name()` replaces `-` with `_` for valid regex group names while preserving the original name in `_name_to_group_map`.

- **[R9] Grouping characters**: Type `n` pattern `\\d{1,3}([.,_]\\d{3})*` supports commas AND underscores as grouping separators.

### Test Results
All 79 existing tests pass with no regressions.

### Pending / Edge Cases
- No remaining requirements are incomplete. All 9 requirements have been addressed and tested.
